content.confidence: 3: You are fairly confident in your assessment. It is possible that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work. Math/other details were not carefully checked.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The authors proposed a GNN architecture that utilized the cached global similarity as an approach to leverage long range dependency in training. CacheGNN comprises serval training tricks to efficiently train and gather global information. Empirical results across several real-world dataset show the effeteness of method.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Pros: 
- Enhance exiting methods with global information hence works on both inductive and transduction settings. 
- Caching previous iterations’ embedding to accelerate training. 
- Representatives for reducing the storage and computation complexity of global information while inference. 


Cons:
- Global similarity is retrieved from output of GNN, error may accumulated and the benefits will be minimum (no extra information is added). 
- The hypothesis of exiting a set of representative nodes and its prior distribution is lack of justification and only supported by empirical results. 
- Trade-off hyperparameter \ita. influent the results a lot and number of global similar nodes are very limited (K = 1 or 2), which make me doubt the usefulness of such information. 
- Time complexity of the algorithm? 
- Compare to other global method like PPNP and GPRGNN? 
- Missing boldface font in table 2.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib: The paper is well written and easy to understand. The idea of incorporating long-range interaction is widely studied in the community and the proposed method is lacking justification to further improve it. There are some empirical novelty in training trick but most of the hypothesis and assumptions are a bit arbitrary and only have empirical support. The codes are publicly available so it should be easy to reproduce.
content.summary_of_the_review: Overall, I would not recommend this paper for acceptance. My concerns about the method includes: the is no guideline on choosing the similarity function, and wether or not the global information defined by them is beneficial is unclear. Same case for the balancing factor \ita. The method feels like will take a lot of trial and error and hyper-parameter tuning. I would also like to see a comparison of method applied to heterophilous/homophilous graphs to see what type of similarity function/long range interaction is useful. The current results are somewhat inconclusive to me.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: This paper proposed CacheGNN, a new GNN model that leverage global similar nodes to enhance existing GNNs. Considering computational cost, the global similar nodes are retrieved from cache of embeddings. To further improve the efficiency, the global similar nodes are selected based on sparse node selection distribution. Experiments showed that the added CacheGNN module can improve various vanilla GNN backbones in both inductive and transductive settings.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths
1.	Leveraging global information to enhance GNN is well explored, but the proposed method based on selected global similar nodes is still new. It is not using the selected global nodes to help with message passing to update embeddings. Instead, only the label information of these nodes is used to enhance the label prediction. Considering this, it is rather a combination of GNN and label propagation (maybe similar to the idea of [1]).
2.	Good experimental performance compared to vanilla GNNs.
3.	Organization of the paper is good. The main idea is easy to follow.

Weakness
1.	Although the method is kind of new, I feel there are a lot of redundance in the model design and many assumptions or modules may not be necessary. For example, the node representations do not need to be a Gaussian distribution, they can be just deterministic embeddings and it can make the inference easier and saves much computational cost. Only \pi and t_u need to be distributions, and they may be not impacted if nodes are not distributions. 
2.	It is not necessary to select the global similar nodes. We can just cache the similarity \phi(z_u, \hat{z}_v) in each iteration. After all, only the labels of these global nodes are used, their embeddings are only used to calculate the similarity to the target nodes.
3.	 I did not check the correctness of (6), but it is important. The ELBO inference process should be described in Appendix.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1.	Equation (3) is not so Bayesian. z_u and t_u are not independent, so this equation looks a little problematic to me. But I understand its motivation and it is not wrong. 
2.	In the Gaussian distribution of N(z_u|GNN(X, \epsilon), \sigma_1^2 I), it seems the GNN output is a matrix instead of a mean vector. It does not seem a correct expression to me.
content.summary_of_the_review: In general, the proposed method provides an interesting idea, but I am worried about its usefulness and significance.
content.correctness: 2: Several of the paper’s claims are incorrect or not well-supported.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.

content.confidence: 4: You are confident in your assessment, but not absolutely certain. It is unlikely, but not impossible, that you did not understand some parts of the submission or that you are unfamiliar with some pieces of related work.
content.summary_of_the_paper: The author points out that leveraging the information from neighboring nodes of traditional GNN methods is subjected to limitations on the space proximity, i.e., only a limited range of neighbors are utilized. In this case, the node embedding may not be fully informative for lack of global features. Hence, this paper proposes a cache-based method to store a subset of important global nodes so that the prediction can be made based on both the local and global attributes. Experiments are conducted to prove the effectiveness of this framework and how the hyper-parameters affect the accuracy.
content.strength_and_weaknesses:
Strengths: 
1. The author of this paper aims to use cached global embedding to achieve higher accuracy. This is a reasonable hypothesis, and this paper verifies the effectiveness of employing both local and global features can help. 

2. Intensive experiments have been conducted. Both transductive and inductive tasks are covered and seven datasets have been used in the experimental parts. Besides, researchers carried out further experiments to learn the effect of the number of global similar nodes K and the trade-off hyper-parameter η.

3. This paper clearly presents the framework with the help of abundant plots and mathematical formulas. The derivation of the EM algorithm and the sampling distribution of selecting similar nodes are explained in detail.


Weaknesses:
1. The datasets are outdated. Five of the seven datasets are citation networks. The remaining two are small Amazon product co-purchase networks. More recent and large benchmark datasets are needed to make the results more convincing. 

2. There are many GNN models proposed every year. There are six baselines, i.e., GATv2Conv (Brody et al., 2021), GCNII (Chen et al., 2020), SGC (Wu et al., 2019), GAT(Velickovicetal.,2018), GraphSAGE (Hamilton et al., 2017), GCN (Kipf & Welling, 2017). The experimental results will be more convincing if we include more state-of-the-art GNN models.

3. What are the connections and differences between the CacheGNN and clustering-based GNNs? E.g., Multi-Channel Graph Neural Networks. Learning a high-level node to represent nodes in the same cluster, may be similar to caching global nodes.

4. One claimed contribution is that the proposed framework can improve prediction efficiency. But there is no experimental result to support this claim.

5. Although one of the key arguments in this paper is about introducing a sparse distribution π to denote the probability of becoming a representative node so as to shrink the size of the cached embedding,  I noticed that some cached sizes still exceed half of the total number of nodes. That means encountering storage difficulties is still possible when dealing with large graphs. I would like to know whether the cached size could be further decreased and see if the accuracy will be sensitive to the cached size. However, the author did not answer these two questions.

6. There exist some other approaches in dealing with the issue that only a limited range of neighbors are utilized, such as the adaptive graph learning method. For instance, it can also be a feasible choice to learn an adaptive graph structure so that the node embedding can learn from the information of other nodes which are not originally located nearby. Besides, some previous studies also focus on aggregating the global information of the graph. But the author merely compared his method with the simplest GNN structure. I doubt whether this method can outperform other related approaches.
content.clarity,_quality,_novelty_and_reproducib:
1. Overall, the author clearly stated his motivation and method in this paper.

2. The author gives a detailed mathematical derivation and probability density function when interpreting the mechanism of the model. The usage of notation is clear, and some key descriptions are also provided in the appendix.

3. In terms of novelty, although the Bayesian method and EM algorithm are commonplace in machine learning related fields, it’s fresh to be used here to select the similar global features of each node. 

4. This method can serve as an additional part, and it is flexible to be implemented into the existing framework.
content.summary_of_the_review: This paper discusses the limitation of traditional GNN related tasks and the importance of utilizing global embedding. Also, the author presents his method to achieve it. At least this paper provides us with some insights in this direction. However, whether this approach can be computationally available when dealing with large graphs and whether this approach can outperform other advanced methods remain to be explored.
content.correctness: 3: Some of the paper’s claims have minor issues. A few statements are not well-supported, or require small changes to be made correct.
content.technical_novelty_and_significance: 3: The contributions are significant and somewhat new. Aspects of the contributions exist in prior work.
content.empirical_novelty_and_significance: 2: The contributions are only marginally significant or novel.
